case_results.diagnosis: The changed line and len(None) counterexample were available, but the external Werkzeug Rule.subdomain nullability contract was not available in the Flask checkout.
Workers found the conversion-error behavior; Critic treated tests and documentation added by the same PR as independent counter-evidence.
The model returned malformed JSON; this is recorded as an execution failure, not a semantic miss.
One worker exhausted its budget; the other refuted only the utility-module aliases and did not resolve the direct get_binary_stream import path named by the review label.
The evidence-resolution protocol forced a candidate with repository type evidence. Lead accepted it, while Critic kept it out of automatic publication pending stronger reachability evidence.
Reviewer, Critic, Lead and evidence gate agreed on the decorator-order defect. The predicted severity was high while the label was medium.

interpretation: This checkpoint combines diagnostic runs made while the implementation was changing and must not be presented as a uniform six-case benchmark.
It proves one formal ordinary-logic hit and one suggestion-level recovery, while exposing remaining cross-dependency, critic-evidence, output-format, and latency gaps.
Run all six cases again from one commit before making an aggregate precision or recall claim.
